title: wiretap: routines to generate "Exported PDU" data
description:
Wiretap currently has three file format readers (busmaster, candump,
nettrace-3gpp) which generate the packet data in Wireshark's "Exported
PDU" encapsulation, because some information (eg, IP addresses) comes
from metadata within the file format, and not from an actual IP header
in the data itself.

This change proposes an API within wiretap which file format readers can
use to generate valid "Exported PDU" packets and their data. Since it
handles bounds checking, padding, etc., it results in a vast reduction
in LoC, and thus complexity, in the modules. This will also enable
future file format readers to more easily do the same thing.

The new routines rely on the `Buffer` type and associated routines as
defined in `wsutil/buffer.h`.

This appears to be a logic error. In the case where the passed-in buffer is non-empty, this stomps over its existing data. It hasn't been a problem until now because all the filetype readers only call `wtap_read_packet_bytes()` on an empty buffer.

In testing this MR with a new file type reader ([rtpdump, if you're curious](https://gitlab.com/boolean263/wireshark/-/commit/8e52dfb75c832cea6daa7d5536437d1e65d8498d)), I was adding Exported-PDU tags to the buffer, then calling `wtap_read_packet_bytes()` to add the raw data which should follow. This change allows that to work.

The comment on `ws_buffer_assure_space()` says to call `ws_buffer_increase_length()` after writing to the end of the buffer, so I thought its absence here was another oversight like the start-vs-end thing. But apparently that's not the right thing to do in this case because adding the `ws_buffer_increase_length()` call causes a whole whack of tests to fail. I'll need to dig deeper.

The problem goes away when I add a call to `ws_buffer_clean()` in `wtap_read()`/`wtap_seek_read()` before the functions pass the buffer to the file subtype for population. I guess my switch to using `ws_buffer_end_ptr()` here broke some assumptions through the code that a buffer would only be written to at the start. I still don't know how increasing the buffer length triggered the test failures I was seeing.

changes_data.diff:
@@ -2209,6 +2209,43 @@ gboolean wtap_dump_close(wtap_dumper *wdh, gboolean *needs_reload,
 WS_DLL_PUBLIC
 gboolean wtap_dump_can_write(const GArray *file_encaps, guint32 required_comment_types);
 
+/**
+ * Generates arbitrary packet data in "exported PDU" format
+ * and appends it to buf.
+ * For filetype readers to transform non-packetized data.
+ * Calls ws_buffer_asssure_space() for you and handles padding
+ * to 4-byte boundary.
+ *
+ * @param[in,out] buf   Buffer into which to write field
+ * @param epdu_tag      tag ID of field to create
+ * @param data          data to be written
+ * @param data_len      length of data
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+void wtap_buffer_append_epdu_tag(Buffer *buf, guint16 epdu_tag, guint8 *data, guint16 data_len);
+
+/**
+ * Generates packet data for an unsigned integer in "exported PDU" format.
+ * For filetype readers to transform non-packetized data.
+ *
+ * @param[in,out] buf   Buffer into which to write field
+ * @param epdu_tag      tag ID of field to create
+ * @param val           integer value to write to buf
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+void wtap_buffer_append_epdu_uint(Buffer *buf, guint16 epdu_tag, guint32 val);
+
+/**
+ * Close off a set of "exported PDUs" added to the buffer.
+ * For filetype readers to transform non-packetized data.
+ *
+ * @param[in,out] buf   Buffer into which to write field
+ *
+ * @return Total length of buf populated to date
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+gint wtap_buffer_append_epdu_end(Buffer *buf);
+
